result.text:
Oakhurst Components Ltd is showing early signs of cash strain on a large and growing exposure. As at 2026-08-31 the buyer had 5 open invoices with Nordhaven Trade Credit (CL05), the worst of which, INV001413 for EUR 329,100, is 25 days past due; a further four invoices totalling EUR 1,220,700 were not yet due. Total open exposure of EUR 1,549,800 already exceeds the EUR 1,450,000 credit limit held on the buyer, by roughly EUR 99,800. Only one settled invoice exists on file, paid on time, so the payment trend is recorded as insufficient_history. On 2026-09-20, Business Dispatch reported that workers at the Birmingham plant staged a protest over delayed wage payments, with union representatives warning of further action if dues are not cleared - read as an indicator of severe cash flow distress.

The score is 47.7, placing the buyer in the Watch band, with a PD of 0.3767. The trace is 0.65 x 33.3 (payment, 25 DPD) + 0.35 x 74.3 (news) = 47.7, giving a weighted payment contribution of 21.7 and a weighted news contribution of 26.0 from the severity 5 wage_delay article, aged 5 days. The adjudicator agreed with caveats: the formula is applied correctly and Watch is defensible, but the band rests almost entirely on the news item, since the payment score of 21.7 alone would fall in the Healthy band. That article is a two-sentence, uncorroborated stub from a single publication, though the entity match is direct rather than via parent and the Birmingham location is consistent. The adjudicator also notes the payment input reads only the 25 DPD and is structurally blind to the limit breach, and that the 2026-08-31 payment snapshot predates the 2026-09-20 news event by about three weeks, so the 33.3 payment score may understate current condition.

The recommendation for Nordhaven Trade Credit (LIM0036) is FREEZE: the current limit of EUR 1,450,000 is held unchanged at a revised limit of EUR 1,450,000, a change of 0, on the grounds that the buyer is already owed at or above the limit and there is nothing left to cut. Expected loss is unchanged at EUR 417,854 before and after. PD of 0.3767 sits above the target of 0.25, and the maximum liability constraint does not bind. This is the only insurer covering this buyer.

Two things would lift this file. First, confirmation or rebuttal of the wage-delay report against a second source: it supplies 26.0 of the 47.7 points, so a signal that fails to corroborate would remove the sole basis for the Watch placement. Second, a refreshed payment position - the current snapshot predates the news event, and the underwriter should establish whether any of the EUR 1,220,700 not-yet-due pipeline has since fallen due, whether the EUR 329,100 past-due item has cleared, and whether exposure has been brought back within the EUR 1,450,000 limit. Additional settled invoices would also build the payment history needed to replace the insufficient_history trend, which currently means the payment component carries less evidential weight in either direction than the raw 33.3 implies.
